_about: ShadowVeil (Alpha 0.4.0): the permanent 1,072 x 1,072 world. Transcribed from projectrpg.txt WORLD BUILDING, which has the final say. Coordinates are the document's: [x, z] 1-based chunks, x west to east, z south to north; a point is the middle of its chunk, fractions are allowed. Heights are block layers (Y). Ranges [x0, x1, z0, z1] are inclusive chunks. Nothing here is code: the generator reads it all.

coast._about: Ocean on all four edges and every corner. The outer two chunks are the shore belt (shelves, coves, shallows, beaches); inland the ground blends up to the regions over 'blend' blocks.

scarp._about: The northern scarp between the Dimwater plateau and Severian's band: a cliff line broken by valleys. Lift is how far the plateau stands proud of the blend at the line; gaps are the valleys and ramps.

roads._about: Main roads connect into loops. 'grade' is the most a road rises per block; 'bridge' is the deck material over water.

kinds._towns: (0.4.1) the settlements' own streets (lamps: a lamp post every so many cells along them), the lanes from doors to the roads, the stone stairways

biomes._about: Per biome: the top block, the soil under it and how deep, the rock below, the face of steep ground, and the trees (species: share of columns).

trees._about: Each species: its log and leaves blocks, trunk height range, crown shape and size. The woodcutting node it becomes is named by 'node' (the devmap's kinds).

outcrops._about: Ore and stone at the surface where the document puts it (Progression & Resources): each a cluster of rocks in a range, how many, and the mineral (rpg.item.Minerals).

mists._about: Banks of ground mist the volumetric march draws (thickest at dawn, dusk, night and in the wet): each a place, how far round it they lie (chunks), how many banks, their size (cells), their height over the ground or water, density and colour.

fishery._about: (0.4.2, gamefixes: fishers did not fish) what lives in each kind of fishing water named above - its stock of each kind of fish - and how far round a spot its water reaches (cells). The devmap keeps its own waters; on ShadowVeil every fishing spot is a water of its kind.
fishery._aboutAll: (0.4.3) every water of the map holds fish: the map in tiles of 'tile' cells, a tile with at least 'minCells' water cells a water of the kind most of them are (the sea by its depth: up to 'shoreDepth' the shore, from 'deepDepth' offshore, the coast between), stocked as that kind is above in proportion to its cells (full stock at 'fullCells')

realms._about: Whose law holds where (settled cores; the rest is the wilds). city, town and empire are the three that keep a lawman (the devmap's DevCity, DevTown and DevPalace).
realms._tint: Each realm's grade (projectrpg.txt 'Visual Tint'): day r, g, b, night r, g, b, fog thickness - blended in across 'blend' cells. The wilds' is the ground everywhere else.

wilds._fogDensity: (0.4.7, gamefixes: fog did not change by region) how thick each biome's air is: the mist's density and how near the bank comes, x1 = the default

realms._fog: (0.4.4, gamefixes: fog tinted by the region you are in) each realm's fog colour (a multiplier on the hour's fog), blended in over its bounds as its tint is; the wilds' by the biome under the eye (wilds.fogBiomes), a neutral one where none is named

places._about: Named places from projectrpg.txt, by key: [x, z] chunk, realm. People are sent to these when they come to ShadowVeil.

transfer._about: Where each of the devmap's people goes on ShadowVeil (0.4.0 has no buildings: they keep their roles and live round the place named). Rules are tried in order; the first whose fields all match wins. Match on 'id' (Ids constant), 'role' (Npc.Role), 'profession' (Profession), 'jurisdiction' (the devmap town the person belonged to: city, town, empire, wilds) or 'name'.

fauna._about: Where the devmap's wildlife goes on ShadowVeil: each animal habitat (rpg.animal.Habitat id) moves whole to a place, its herds and packs keeping their shape; each monster kind's lair (rpg.monster.MonsterKind) to the place its kind lives.

wilds._about: (0.4.3, gamefixes: wildlife throughout the whole world, and logically: no predators near the towns) the wild's own habitats, grown over the whole square: a sample point every 'grid' cells, a habitat 'size' across about it, its animals the groups its biome lists ([species, females, males, young, percent chance]). Prey keeps 'prey' cells clear of any building; a group with a predator in it lives only where the wilds hold sway (no kingdom's law) and 'predator' cells from any settlement's building. Hysteresis keeps the farms' stock and the towns' strays as they are.
wilds._perches: (0.4.7) the settled places' birds: each kind of structure's groups [species, females, males, young, percent chance], in a habitat 'size' across about it

danger._about: (0.4.8, gamefixes: enemy levels by distance from Loxford) How dangerous the land is (rpg.world.shadowveil.Danger): nothing within 'safe' cells of the 'origin' realm's middle, rising along 'curve' to its full at 'far' cells; each region may add to or take from it. Enemies' levels at a place lie between 'low' and 'high', each taken at its danger ([at none, at full]): the monsters' territories, the dungeons' residents, the hostile people and beasts of encounters.

monsters._about: (0.4.4, gamefixes: monsters with natural spawn locations and territories in the wilderness - orcs, goblins, the overworld's kinds, not the caves' zombies, skeletons or dragons) A territory grows on the open wilds on a grid (jittered), where its biome holds the kind by its chance, far from every kingdom and homestead ('clearance', cells) and off the roads: its lair (a camp, a nest, a haunt) and the ground its members roam, hunt and return to. Per biome: [kind, lowest level, highest level, how many it holds, chance in a hundred]. Its population is the monster system's own - it breeds when fed and safe, and is not respawned on a timer.
monsters._clearance: cells kept clear: from any building inside a kingdom's bounds ('town'), from a lone building, hall or home out in the wilds ('homestead'), from a road ('road')

gathering._about: (0.4.5, gamefixes: Harvesting did not work - ShadowVeil had nothing wild to gather) The wild's gathering, grown over the whole square like its trees: a point tried every 'grid' cells (jittered), each kind's chance by the biome there; never on a road, a lane, a lot, a yard, water, a cliff or under a tree. Each kind is a Harvesting node of the same rules as anywhere: its level, what it gives, its experience, the time a pick takes, how many picks before it is bare, and the game minutes it takes to grow back.

clearance._about: Kept this far (cells) from a lot and from a road: the gatherer's ground is the wild's.

townTalk._about: (0.4.7) What townsfolk say of their own kingdom, from projectrpg.txt's LORE. Keyed by realm; 'default' for anyone, or by role (GUARD, MERCHANT, PRIEST, CIVIC...). Read by Dialogue in place of hardcoded lines.

default: The harvest dues come before anything else here. Ask anyone who missed them.
Keep to the Sun rites and folk will leave you be. Mostly.
King Richard keeps the old peace, so they say. The roads tell a different story.
Strangers are watched in Loxford. Don't take it to heart.
GUARD: The king's peace holds inside these walls. Outside, mind yourself.
Watchtower's the last of the crown's eyes on the King's Road.
PRIEST: The rites keep the dread off. Come to the church before you need it.

default: A guest is owed bread and a roof. A thief is owed the Sultan's court.
Argue well here and they'll remember your name longer than your coin.
Valgard's ore comes in raw and leaves as craft. That's Azharad's trade.
The scholars will debate anything. Even the price of bread.
MERCHANT: Severian ships carry our finished goods. Their fees are a scandal.

default: Everything worth having passes through the Great Market sooner or later.
Leonidas rules by charters and favours. Know whose favour you hold.
The harbour and the archives - that's what keeps the Empire needed.
Sun church on the hill, Moon shrine by the market. We get along, mostly.
GUARD: Imperial patrol fees keep the roads safe. Mostly.
CIVIC: Records matter here. A thing not written down didn't happen.

default: A knight's oath and a miner's wage are written in the same book here.
The guild families hold the skills. The crown holds the guild families.
King Phillip expects discipline. So does the mine.
Our iron arms half the kingdoms. Nobody thanks us for it.
GUARD: Keep to the law and the law keeps you. That's Valgard.

default: Chieftain Torkell is judged by the winter stores. So far, he's held.
Work earns you a place here. A name doesn't.
A witnessed promise is worth more than ink in Gorrick.
Valgard wants to inspect every northern shipment. Let them try.
Bolt your door at dusk. That's not advice, it's custom.
The count's protection is real. So is the price of it.
We mark births, debts and departures carefully here.
Speak freely by your own hearth. Nowhere else.
At the Round Table every voice gets a hearing. Not every voice gets heeded.
Arthur shelters those who flee. Not every king likes that.
Our escorts guard the roads for less than the imperial patrols ask.
An oath sworn here is sworn in public. Breaking it is public too.
Out here a kept promise is worth more than any title.
Every camp keeps its own rules. Learn them quick.
Hospitality ends at the next ridge, they say. Don't test it.
